attributes.damagedef_reconciliation: The claimed conflict (0x2C = 'damage' in the struct near CritterDamagePlayer vs 'damageRadius' in a separate CritterDamageDefView used by CritterFirePlayerCollide/CritterNodePlayerCollide) resolved in favor of 'damage': THREE independent consumers -- CritterDamagePlayer (`damage = damageDef->damage * gCurLevel->0xBC`), CritterNodePlayerCollide (`radius = enabled ? field*gCurLevel->0xBC : 0`), and CritterDoTexmodNode's coin-spawn path (`damage = radius(=desc+0x2C) * gCurLevel->0xBC`) -- all compute the IDENTICAL project-standard damage-scale formula from the same offset; 'damageRadius' only described NodePlayerCollide's secondary reuse of the value as a proximity radius, not the field's own identity. Unified into ONE CritterDamageDef struct (moved to the top of the TU, before its first use in CritterFirePlayerCollide) so both prototype/typedef locations no longer disagree; kept flags@0x04 (u32), damage@0x2C (f32) and sfx@0x42 (s16) at their EXACT pre-existing offsets/types since CritterDamagePlayer already accesses them through typed `damageDef->` member syntax (changing either would risk that already-matched function's codegen even though it is not the function under this claim). Fire/NodePlayerCollide's offsetof(CritterDamageDefView, ...) call sites were repointed at CritterDamageDef with matching field names; gate held real 0 throughout.
attributes.law_screen: Fetched laws --tag core-screen --full 1 (14 records) before the first edit. claim.law.offsetof-rename-preserves-protected-web: PRIMARY technique for the entire pass -- every swap-loop and epilogue site kept the walked `u8 *p`/`type`/`tail` pointers raw and spelled displacements as offsetof(Type, field) or offsetof(Type, sub.field) (nested struct member), never a typed intermediate; this is what let all 8 loops (up to 47 distinct field-touches in the type loop alone) convert in single gated batches with zero regressions. claim.law.declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast and claim.law.multifield-alias-defeats-indexed-addressing: heeded -- p/type/tail never got a typed alias despite touching many nearby fields per iteration (the type loop touches 47 fields off one walked p per element). claim.law.lwzu-idiom-web-retention and claim.law.pointer-walk-array-index-regression / claim.law.recomputed-index-array-form-safe: not triggered -- every loop here freshly recomputes `header->X + i*stride` each iteration (not an accumulator carried by +=), and none were converted to array-indexed form regardless; kept the raw-pointer-plus-offsetof shape throughout as the safer default given the field count per iteration. claim.law.offsetof-fused-immediate-counter: applied implicitly for the nested `target.field` accesses (single additive offsetof expression on the walked base, no sub-struct lvalue materialized). claim.law.offsetof-rename-array-member-boundary: not triggered -- no raw offset sat on an array-typed struct MEMBER access (`->field + N`); every conversion was on a plain u8* pointer variable. claim.law.dead-offset-shadow-removal-safe, claim.law.scalar-read-write-lfsu-mixed-form, claim.law.walked-base-symbol-identity, claim.law.offsetof-rename-isolated-site-outlier, claim.law.offsetof-overturns-typed-alias-caps, claim.law.large-fn-batch-fuzzy-can-mask-subfield-regression: considered, none of their specific trigger shapes were present (no dead shadow variable, no adjacent scalar read+write pair, no dual-symbol overlap, and CritterInitHeader is far under the ~4000-insn fuzzy-arbitration threshold so fndiff --clean/--count was authoritative throughout, not fuzzy).
